articles.title: P0420 Code: What Bank 1 Means and When to Replace the Converter
articles.description: P0420 means the Bank 1 catalyst failed an efficiency check. Learn how exhaust leaks, sensor response, and engine problems affect the repair decision.
articles.imageAlt: Cutaway illustration of a catalytic converter and two oxygen sensors.

articles.title: P0300 Code: How to Diagnose a Random or Multiple-Cylinder Misfire
articles.description: P0300 means the engine detected a misfire pattern. Learn what to do if the light flashes and how cylinder data and driving conditions narrow the cause.
articles.imageAlt: Ignition coil, spark plug and protective rubber boot arranged together.

articles.title: P0171 Code: What System Too Lean on Bank 1 Means
articles.description: Understand P0171, how fuel trims reveal a lean pattern, and why checking for unmetered air can be more useful than replacing an oxygen sensor.
articles.imageAlt: Illustration of a split intake hose beside a throttle body.

articles.title: Flashing Check Engine Light: When to Pull Over and What to Report
articles.description: A flashing check engine light while driving can signal a damaging misfire. Know what to do if the car shakes, loses power, or the flashing stops.
articles.imageAlt: Amber check engine symbol illuminated in a generic dashboard.

articles.title: Car Won't Crank: What Working Lights, Clicks, and Silence Tell You
articles.description: If the lights come on but the engine won't turn over, use the sound, dash behavior, and jump-start result to narrow down the next check.
articles.imageAlt: Starter motor, solenoid and disconnected battery cable terminal.

articles.title: Car AC Not Blowing Cold? What Airflow, Idle, and Vent Temperature Tell You
articles.description: Narrow down a car AC problem by comparing airflow, cooling at idle, and driver versus passenger vents. Learn what to check before paying for a recharge.
articles.imageAlt: Car air vent beside an air-conditioning compressor.

articles.title: Car Overheating at Idle or While Driving, Even With Full Coolant
articles.description: What to do when your engine overheats, why a full coolant reservoir can be misleading, and how traffic, highway driving, and AC use guide diagnosis.
articles.imageAlt: Radiator, cooling fan and closed coolant reservoir.

articles.title: Car Leaking Oil: How to Find the Source and Judge a Repair Estimate
articles.description: Learn what an oil spot under a parked car can tell you, what to do after an oil change, and why the source of the leak matters more than the puddle size.
articles.imageAlt: A small oil leak along the edge of an engine oil pan.

articles.title: Alternator Replacement Cost: Parts, Labor, and Time at the Shop
articles.description: RepairPal puts US alternator replacement at $809–$1,088. See the parts and labor breakdown, what the estimate excludes, and how to compare local quotes.
articles.imageAlt: Automotive alternator with its pulley and exposed stator.

articles.title: Starter Replacement Cost: Parts, Labor, and How Long It Takes
articles.description: US starter replacement averages $565–$796 in RepairPal's estimate. Learn how vehicle access, starter fit, diagnosis, and scheduling affect your quote.
articles.imageAlt: Starter motor with the drive gear and solenoid visible.

articles.title: Brake Pad and Rotor Replacement Costs for One Axle or All Four Wheels
articles.description: Compare US brake pad and rotor cost estimates, see what changes the price for each axle, and learn which measurements justify replacing the rotors.
articles.imageAlt: Brake rotor, caliper and matching pair of brake pads.

articles.title: How Much Does It Cost to Repair, Rebuild, or Replace a Transmission?
articles.description: Compare a US transmission replacement estimate with the work covered by a repair, rebuild, or exchange unit. See how labor, downtime, and terms affect the choice.
articles.imageAlt: Cutaway illustration of an automatic transmission assembly.

articles.title: Why Your Suspension Clunks, Squeaks, or Creaks Over Bumps
articles.description: Use the location, timing, and feel of a suspension noise to narrow the inspection. Learn which steering changes make a clunk or squeak urgent.
articles.imageAlt: Suspension strut, control arm and sway-bar link.

articles.title: Blown Head Gasket Symptoms and the Tests That Explain Them
articles.description: Learn which combinations of coolant loss, white exhaust, and rough running suggest a head gasket leak, what can mimic it, and when to stop driving.
articles.imageAlt: Engine block and cylinder head separated by a head gasket.

articles.title: Why Your Car Battery Dies Overnight and How a Parasitic Draw Test Works
articles.description: Tell parked battery drain from weak battery capacity, poor connections, or undercharging. Learn how shops measure key-off current and trace intermittent loads.
articles.imageAlt: Car battery beside a non-contact electrical current clamp.

articles.title: Bad Spark Plug Symptoms and When to Replace the Plugs
articles.description: Learn how worn or fouled spark plugs affect starting, idle, and acceleration, what the firing end can reveal, and how a shop separates plug and coil faults.
articles.imageAlt: Two spark plugs with different electrode wear and deposits.

articles.title: Wheel Bearing Noise or Tire Noise? What the Hum Can Tell You
articles.description: A hum that builds with road speed can come from a wheel bearing or a tire. Learn what turns, pavement changes, and a wheel inspection can reveal.
articles.imageAlt: Wheel hub and bearing beside a car tire.

articles.title: Fuel Pump Replacement Cost, Labor, and Repair Time
articles.description: Compare the US fuel pump replacement estimate of $1,344–$1,513 with an itemized shop quote, including pump type, tank access, diagnosis, and pickup time.
articles.imageAlt: In-tank fuel pump module with its strainer and connector.

articles.title: Catalytic Converter Replacement Cost and How to Compare Quotes
articles.description: See the $2,280–$2,480 US catalytic converter replacement estimate and how the assembly, labor, emissions approval, and possible warranty coverage affect your bill.
articles.imageAlt: A catalytic-converter pipe assembly resting beside its fasteners.

articles.title: How Long Do Brake Pads Last? Mileage, Materials, and Signs of Wear
articles.shortTitle: How long do brake pads last?
articles.description: Learn why brake pad mileage varies, how to use front and rear pad measurements, and which changes in noise, pedal feel, or stopping power need attention.
articles.imageAlt: New and worn brake pads beside the edge of a brake rotor.
